Bhagavad Gita, Chapter 2, Verse 2

“The Blessed Lord said: Where has this faintheartedness come from at such a moment, Arjuna? It is unworthy of a noble man, it closes the gate to heaven, and it brings disgrace.”

Krishna's opening move is not comfort but challenge. He names the collapse kashmala — a stain, a clouding — and questions its timing. The teaching begins by refusing to accept despair as wisdom.
